### Bbknn

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obsm_input`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The dimensionality reduction in `.obsm` to use for neighbour detection. Defaults to X_pca.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"X_pca"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_batch`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.obs column name discriminating between your batches.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--uns_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Mandatory .uns slot to store various neighbor output objects.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"bbknn_integration_neighbors"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obsp_distances`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
In which .obsp slot to store the distance matrix between the resulting neighbors.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"bbknn_integration_distances"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obsp_connectivities`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
In which .obsp slot to store the connectivities matrix between the resulting neighbors.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"bbknn_integration_connectivities"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_neighbors_within_batch`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
How many top neighbours to report for each batch; total number of neighbours in the initial k-nearest-neighbours computation will be this number times the number of batches.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `3`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_pcs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
How many dimensions (in case of PCA, principal components) to use in the analysis.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `50`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_trim`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Trim the neighbours of each cell to these many top connectivities. May help with population independence and improve the tidiness of clustering. The lower the value the more independent the individual populations, at the cost of more conserved batch effect. If `None` (default), sets the parameter value automatically to 10 times `neighbors_within_batch` times the number of batches. Set to 0 to skip.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}

::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_cluster`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Prefix for the .obs keys under which to add the cluster labels. Newly created columns in .obs will
be created from the specified value for '--obs_cluster' suffixed with an underscore and one of the resolutions
resolutions specified in '--leiden_resolution'.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"bbknn_integration_leiden"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--leiden_resolution`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Control the coarseness of the clustering. Higher values lead to more clusters.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/bbknn_leiden/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/workflows/integration/bbknn_leiden);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/bbknn_leiden/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
